title: A protocol for extraction and purification of high-quality and quantity bacterial DNA applicable for genome sequencing: a modified version of the Marmur procedure.
protocol: Suspend a fully-loaded inoculating loop of bacterial biomass in an 800 µl EDTA-Saline solution.
Vortex at maximum speed to mix thoroughly.
Add 10 µl of lysozyme.
If Gram-positive bacteria, add 10 µl of mutanolysin.
Mix by vortexing for a few seconds.
Incubate at 37°C for at least 15 – 45 min; vortex every 15 min.
Add 80 µl of SDS.
Vortex at maximum speed for a few seconds.
Incubate at 65°C for 10 min; vortex once during this time.
Spin down briefly and add 250 µl of sodium chloride 5 M.
Vortex at maximum speed for a few seconds and spin down briefly.
Add 400 µl of chloroform:isoamyl alcohol.
Vortex at maximum speed for a few seconds; shake for 15 min at 1,400 rpm on an orbital shaker.
Centrifuge at > 13,000 x g for 15 min.
Transfer the top-layer to a new tube (2 ml); avoid the protein layer.
Add 400 µl of chloroform:isoamyl alcohol again; shake vigorously by hand and centrifuge again.
Repeat step until there is no protein layer.
To 1 ml of solution, add 90 µl of sodium acetate 3 M.
To 1 ml of solution, add 600 µl of cold isopropanol (4°C).
Precipitate the DNA by inverting the tube several times by hand; shake harder to clump the DNA threads when threads are visible.
Spool the DNA using a glass rod.
Leave the spooled DNA to dry completely for at least 5 minutes at room temperature.
If threads do not form, spin down at > 13,000 x g for 10 minutes.
Carefully discard the supernatant after spinning.
Let the DNA pellet dry completely at room temperature.
Suspend the spooled or pelleted DNA in 100 µl of ‘low’-TE.
Incubate the resuspended DNA overnight at 4°C.
